page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.s6-c1m2.xlarge is an entry-tier virtual instance from the shared ecs.s6 family, running on the KVM hypervisor. It is equipped with 4 shared vCPUs derived from an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz. System memory is sized at 8.0 GB, establishing a 1:2 compute-optimized ratio with 2.0 GB of memory per core. The shared CPU allocation model distributes physical host resources among multiple virtual tenants, prioritizing cost efficiency over dedicated hardware reservation.

This configuration includes no bundled local storage, meaning primary persistence relies entirely on remote block storage solutions. It provides no GPU acceleration resources and lacks complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The baseline network bandwidth is designated at 0 Gbps, reflecting its positioning within shared resource pools. Additionally, the instance reports unexposed extended CPU features and vector accelerators in its guest environment.

The structural tradeoff of the ecs.s6-c1m2.xlarge centers on CPU sharing. While the 4 vCPU to 8 GB memory ratio handles multi-threaded tasks well, potential contention on shared cores makes it unsuitable for latency-sensitive production systems. It is most appropriate for staging environments, automated testing, lightweight microservices, internal CI/CD runners, and background batch tasks where low infrastructure overhead is prioritized over guaranteed throughput.
